The automobile transport business of this segment, together with the Energy Business, contributed to the group's overall revenue growth. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, crude oil tanker market conditions remained at high levels from September onward, when cargo volumes increased following the lifting of voluntary production cuts by OPEC+ countries. For product tankers, market conditions for large vessels were firm, while for LPG carriers, trade became more complex due to US port fee measures and US-China tariff issues, and ton-miles increased. For chemical tankers, market conditions softened due to uncertainty in the global economy.

Panamax and smaller vessels were supported by cargo movements of grain, coal and minor bulks.
